items: A flame the size of a match head sits on your thumb whenever you want it. It lights candles, pipes and stubborn stoves, and it goes out in a stiff breeze.
Puddles, wet grass and shallow water part under each footfall, one step at a time, so your feet stay dry. It works in water up to ankle depth.
You can whistle in the exact voice of any bird you have heard. It fools people completely and fools the birds themselves for about a minute.
Whatever you hold cools to just above freezing within a minute. Drinks, fevered foreheads and fish on a hot dock are all fair game. It works on one thing at a time and nothing bigger than a bucket.
Tie a knot in any cord while you think of a sentence, and whoever unties it hears the sentence in your voice. Each knot holds about ten words and keeps for a year.
Once a day you can put off being tired. The exhaustion waits one hour and then hits you all at once, worse than it would have been.
Make and steer ordinary fire. You start with a campfire's worth within arm's reach. You are not immune to it and can be burned by your own flames.
Pull water out of damp air and send it where you like. A bathtub's worth obeys you at first. It stays plain water and falls as soon as you stop paying attention.

Lay a palm on worked stone and ask it one question about what has happened near it. Stone answers honestly but slowly, and it knows only what it felt: weight, footsteps, heat and vibration. It cannot see or hear.
Either arm stretches to three times its length and keeps its full strength the whole way out.

Call weather over a town-sized patch of sky. Asking takes an hour, and you get whatever the season allows pushed as far as it will go: a summer shower turns into a thunderstorm, a frost into a blizzard.
Open any door you have touched before from any other door within a mile. The two doorways are one doorway for as long as you hold the handle, and anything can walk through from either side.
Your skin hardens into living wood on command, thick enough to stop a rifle round. You move slower while it lasts.
Take the sound out of a space the size of a city block. Nothing inside can be heard, you included, for as long as you can hold your breath plus one minute.

Rivers move for you. Turn one out of its bed, stand it up as a wall, or send a season's flood down a dry valley. The water has to exist already, and it returns to its old course when you stop holding it.
For a minute at a time, every blow you throw lands a hundred times across everything in front of you. One punch clears a street. The arm you used is useless for a day afterward.
Wear the face, voice and build of anyone whose hand you have shaken. It holds until you sleep. You get none of their memories.

Name a thing or a person and feel exactly where it is, anywhere within a few hundred miles, along with the shortest way there. Things that were deliberately hidden register only as somewhere in range, with no direction.
Strike the ground and choose where the fault opens. At full strength the crack runs from one border of a country to the other and takes the mountain passes with it. The fault is permanent.
Draw a line of light from your fingertip to the horizon. Everything along it is as hot as the surface of the sun for one second. You can draw the next line after a slow count of sixty.
Split into as many as a thousand of yourself, each one entirely you. They share what they learned when they fold back together, and any that died bring the memory of dying home with them.
Speak one sentence as law, and a whole country follows it for a day without wondering why. It cannot make anyone harm themselves, and you get one sentence a month.
The oceans answer you. Raise a wave that crosses a continent, or pull the sea back from a coast until the shelf lies bare. The water you move away from one coast floods another.
One step takes you anywhere on the planet that you can name. Anyone holding your hand comes along. Places that have never had a name stay out of reach until somebody gives them one.
Point at something no larger than a mountain and it stops existing, with no debris and no noise. People still remember it was there. This works once per sunrise and never on anything alive.
You can move a planet's moon at will. Tides, orbits and eclipses happen when you decide. If you release it carelessly it falls or flies off, and you will not be able to catch it in time.
Change one fact about the world by saying what is true in its place. The planet rearranges itself to fit, history included, and only you remember the earlier draft. One sentence a year.
Light a star wherever there is enough dust to make one, or put one out. Either takes a day of concentration. Putting one out leaves its planets dark and frozen.
Distance stops applying to you. You arrive anywhere in the galaxy at the moment you decide to leave, along with whatever and whoever you could see when you went.
Whatever you say about the universe becomes the case, at any scale, for as long as you keep saying it. Only your own later statements can undo an earlier one.
A breeze about as strong as a paper fan blows from your open palm for as long as you hold it up. It is enough to dry ink or cool soup.
Look at anyone's back and you know exactly where it itches.

Your hands are always warm, and by touch you can tell where a person is tense, where they are ticklish and where they like to be touched during sex. It tells you nothing about whether they want you to.
Run a thumb along a tear in cloth and it closes, thread by thread. A ripped sleeve takes a few seconds and a shredded sail takes an afternoon. It works only on woven cloth.
Anything that leaves your hand falls at the speed of a drifting feather, if you want it to. Cups, eggs and small children on low walls all land softly.
Touch a willing partner anywhere on their body and that spot becomes as sensitive as their genitals for as long as your fingers stay there. It stops the moment they want it to.
Glass holds you like a floor, at any angle. You can stroll up a shopfront, cross a greenhouse roof or stand on the inside of a window looking down at the street.
Cup your hands around any sound and you have caught it. Open them later and it plays back once, at full volume. You can hold three sounds at a time.
Roots drive from your heels into whatever you stand on, including stone. While they hold, a charging horse will not shift you and a gale will not lean you over.

While you are having sex with a willing partner, each of you feels the other's arousal and orgasms as well as your own. At first this makes both of you come quickly. With practice you can hold each other at the edge for hours.
For three steps at a time, nothing solid stops you. Walls, locked doors and the side of a moving train are all open country. Stop inside something and you are pushed out the way you came, bruised.
Iron and steel within a hundred paces come to your open hand or leap away from your closed fist. Swords leave scabbards, locks tear out of doors, and a rifle volley curves off into the trees.

Fall asleep thinking of a lover who is thinking of you, and the two of you meet in a dream that either can shape. Sex there feels exactly as it does awake, at any distance, and you both remember it in the morning.
Every insect in a town answers you. Bees will carry a message cell by cell, locusts will spare one field and strip the next, and a cloud of midges can hide a street.
Shout at a hillside and it comes down. Snow, scree, a cliff face or the upper storeys of a fortress, anywhere within sight, will let go at one word from you.
Step into any mirror big enough to admit you and out of any other mirror in the region that you have looked into before.

You can raise or lower sexual arousal in everyone within sight, yourself included. It works only on attraction a person already feels. You can leave a couple who want each other unable to wait until they get home, or cool a lust that is about to start a fight. It cannot make anyone want a person they do not want.
Lay hands on one sick person and name the disease. The cure passes from them to everyone they touch, and onward, until the illness is gone from the region. It takes about a month to run its course.
Reach up and pull, and anything in the sky over a country comes down where you point: a flock, an airship, a hailstorm, a falling star caught before it lands.
Every edged weapon within a mile leaves its owner and flies for you. They hang in the air at your shoulder like a shoal, and go where you look.

Sing, and every adult in the country who hears it becomes sexually aroused and thinks of you. Nobody is compelled to act. Many of them masturbate to the thought of you that night, and a good number come looking for you in person.
Ask a forest to walk and it does. Trees pull up their roots and move at a steady march to wherever in the country you send them, and stand there as if they had grown on the spot.
Cut the air with the edge of your hand and the weather over a continent splits along the line. One side gets the cloud, the other gets the clear sky, and it stays that way until you undo it.
Once a week you can live a day again from its dawn, keeping what you learned. Everyone else on the continent lives it again without knowing. You get one second attempt per day and no third.

Once a season you can give an orgasm to every adult on a continent who would welcome one at that moment. It lasts about a minute and arrives wherever they happen to be. Everyone who would not want it feels nothing.
Put your shoulder to a continent and it moves. A year of steady pushing can close a strait, open an ocean or bring two coasts together that have not touched in an age.
At a word, every ocean on the planet goes still and solid as a mirror, safe to walk or ride across. At another word the water is water again. Ships caught in it are held fast but unharmed.
You decide what falls toward what. Planets leave their orbits when you call them, suns come to heel, and anything you let go of flies off in a straight line until you call it back.
You can speak one sentence into every mind in the galaxy at once, in words each of them understands. They know it came from you. Choose the sentence with care, since you can send only one a year.
Wipe the universe clean, down to the first blank moment, and start it again. This time you watch from outside, and you can reach in whenever you choose.
A walking stick, shoulder high, cut from ash. It is exactly as good as any stick, and it never gives you a splinter.
A plain butter knife with a grand inscription nobody has managed to translate. It spreads butter well. It cuts nothing else.
A leather sling and a bag of twelve river stones. The bag is full again each morning. It gives no help with your aim.
A short oak club with a wrist loop. Anyone struck with it stays down for the count of ten and has no lasting harm to show for it afterward.
A hooked pole that floats, never rusts, and always comes back up from the bottom within reach of your hand.
A hammer that is also, when you need it, a wrench, a pry bar or a screwdriver of the right size. It changes while you are not looking at it.
A round shield made from an old kitchen table. While you stand in a doorway with it, nothing that means harm to the people behind you gets through that door short of knocking down the wall.
A green-bladed dagger. Any scratch from it burns and swells like a bed of nettles for an hour, enough to make a grown soldier drop what he is holding.
A long spear with a caged flame below the blade. Its light shows things as they are, so disguises and illusions inside its circle are plainly visible as fakes.
A worn revolver with the maker's mark filed off. It holds six shots, reloads itself at dawn, and has never once jammed or misfired.
A two-handed maul with an iron head the size of a bread oven. It is weightless in your hands and strikes with its full weight. One swing opens a castle gate.
A stoppered clay jar with one bolt of lightning inside. Pull the stopper and point the mouth. By the next morning the jar has collected another one.
A steel needle on a mile of grey thread. It flies where you look and sews what it touches: wounds closed, doors shut, a running man's coat to the wall.
A bolt-action rifle with a brass scope. Whatever you can see through the scope you can hit, at any distance and in any wind. You load each round by hand.
A knight's longsword that cannot be drawn in a cause you believe is wrong. In one you believe is right, it cuts through stone walls and plate armour, and no one can strike it from your hand.
A black fan of crow feathers. A wave of it sends a wind down the valley that rots wood, rusts iron and ages whatever it touches by ten years. It affects friends and enemies alike.
A spear tipped with a tooth as long as a forearm. Thrown, it goes through anything in a straight line for a full mile and then returns to your hand.
Nine field guns on self-driving carriages that follow you and fire where you point. They do not supply their own shells.
A plain sword with a crown worked into the pommel. Whoever you fight for with it will rule the country at the end of the war, and armies lose heart at the sight of it raised.
A glaive of blue ice that never melts. Its swing sends a killing frost fifty miles in the direction you cut. The frost destroys crops and freezes harbours along its whole path.
A cannon the length of a train, on a rail carriage that lays its own track. It lands a shell on any point in a country to within a pace. Loading takes the full crew of forty that comes with it.
An iron chain that is as long as you need it to be. It can bind a river in its bed, hold a collapsing mountain together, or haul down anything that flies, and it has never broken.
A javelin of white fire. Thrown, it lands as a second sunrise and leaves a glass plain where an army stood, across a front as wide as a continent's coast. It reforms in your hand the next day.
An axe with a head of dull grey metal that nothing scratches. A full swing opens a canyon from sea to sea. You can also use it with fine control at any smaller scale.
A hand bell with no clapper. When you ring it, everyone on the continent who is holding a weapon in anger puts it down and cannot remember why they picked it up. It works once per war.
A silver bow strung with light. Its arrows reach anything under the same sky, including the things in that sky, and a full draw puts a crater on the far side of the world.
A smith's hammer the size of an anvil. One blow on bare rock starts a volcano. A sustained beat reshapes a planet's crust like sheet copper, and anything made under it never wears out.
A black glass sceptre that calls down stars. Name the target and one arrives. The impact destroys whatever planet it lands on.
Ten thousand warships crewed by their own engines, mothballed in a pocket of space until you call. Together they can hold every lane in a galaxy. They obey one admiral, and the rank is yours.
A pen with one drop of ink in it. The mark it makes ends whatever sentence it is placed after: a life, a war, a law of nature, a universe. The drop is back by the next day.
A heavy beech rolling pin. It makes good pastry and works as a club.
A tin tube and a pocketful of dried peas. You never miss the back of a neck at twenty paces. The peas are replaced overnight.
A long ostrich plume on an ebony handle, made for teasing a naked partner. It finds the most sensitive place on anyone's body within three strokes.
A forked stick of apple wood with a strip of leather. It throws a stone hard enough to stun a hare or crack a window across a river.
Eight feet of ash with a bronze hook and spike. It holds off boarders and fends off quays, and it brings back whatever fell overboard on the first cast.
A slim leather crop for spanking a willing partner. Each stroke hurts exactly as much as the person receiving it wants, and the marks are gone by morning. It does nothing to horses.
A short dark bow that makes no sound at all. The string is silent, the arrow flies without a hiss, and whatever it hits drops without crying out.
A flanged mace with a bronze bell for a head. Each blow rings, and everyone who hears the note is certain for a minute afterward that you are in the right.
A flintlock small enough for a sleeve. No search finds it and no damp spoils the powder. It holds one shot.

Four lengths of red silk rope for tying up a lover. The knots hold against any strength and fall open the instant the bound person truly wants out. They never chafe, and they will not hold anyone who did not agree to be tied.
A whaler's iron on an endless line. It goes through a ship's hull as easily as blubber, and the line hauls in whatever is on the end without help from you.
Twelve feet of braided wire that cracks with white fire. It cuts through a lamp post, lights whatever it wraps around, and can pick a pistol out of a hand across a room.

Three gold-tipped arrows that draw no blood. Anyone struck becomes intensely aroused for the person they already desire most and wants sex with them at once. The arrows cannot point that lust at anyone new.
A steel crossbow with a crank and a hopper. It puts sixty bolts a minute through a shield wall and can be worked one-handed.
A length of lightning-struck oak. Plant it and a thunderhead builds overhead. Point it and the bolts walk wherever you direct them, across a region, for as long as you stand there.
A farm scythe with a blade the colour of old pewter. One sweep takes down everything standing in a field: wheat, pikes, a rank of cavalry. Whatever falls to it never gets up as a ghost.
A matched pair. Throw one and it flies to wherever the other is, through anything in the way. A fighter holding both can be on either side of a regiment as it suits.
A squat bronze siege mortar on a sledge. Its bombs fall straight down on anything you have seen from a height, walls or no walls, at a range of thirty miles.

A many-tailed whip of black velvet cord. To anyone who wants to submit sexually to its wielder, each stroke feels like the edge of orgasm, and they will kneel and ask for more. On anyone who does not want that, it is a soft rope and nothing else. Whole companies of soldiers have laid down their arms for it.
Green bronze, crusted with barnacles. Strike a shore with it and the sea comes inland for fifty miles. Strike the sea and a road opens across the bottom, dry between two walls of water.
A yew bow that takes a hundred years to make. An arrow from it crosses a country and hits a target the size of a nail head.
A torn standard on a spear shaft. No army that marches under it can be routed, starved into surrender or bought. They may still lose, but only by dying where they stand.
A spear with the dawn for a blade. Thrown at sunrise, it rides the daybreak line west across a whole continent and strikes every enemy you named before you threw it.
A sword as long as a ship's mast, which you can swing like a switch. It takes the top off a mountain range in one stroke.
A sceptre of red gold. Raise it and every crowned head on the continent feels a hand on their shoulder. They can refuse you, but each of them knows what you have asked and that you are watching.
A gun the size of a mountain, dug into a moon. One shot cracks a world. It takes a day to charge and a staff of ten thousand to fire.
A blade of grey light. A single sweep ends one kind of thing across a whole world: a plague, a species of weed, every sword. It takes a year to return, and what it reaped does not come back.
A lance ground from the core of a dead sun. Couched and charged, it goes through a planet, the moon behind it and the star behind that, and is clean when you pull it out.
Twelve engines that each hold a collapsed star on a chain. Fired together they open a wound in space that swallows a fleet, a world or a sun, and closes neatly behind it.
An editor's pencil, sharpened at both ends. Draw a line through anything at all, a person, a nation, a force of nature, a universe, and it is struck from the text as if it had never been set down.
The end of a good loaf, still warm. It is enough for one meal for one person and it is back in your bag each morning.
A copper coin. Spend it, and the next coin toss, card cut or dice roll you make goes your way. It works once.
A small white sweet that clears your breath, your sinuses and your head for an hour. The tin holds one at a time.
A tin of green paste. Spread on a cut, a burn or a sprain, it does a week of healing overnight. One tin treats about five injuries.
One paper twist of black tea. A cup of it keeps you walking through a day and a night without food or sleep. Afterward you need a full day of rest and a large meal.
A stub of white chalk. A line drawn across a threshold with it keeps out rats, insects and draughts until the line is scuffed.
A glass vial with a grey mist in it. Break it and you get sixty seconds in which nothing else moves. You can't hurt anyone during it, but you can leave.
A flask of clear spirit that tastes of smoke. One mouthful lets you breathe a jet of flame as long as a room, once. Only the first mouthful from each flask works.
A worn silver coin. Put it under the tongue of someone who died within the day and they will answer three questions truthfully before they go quiet again.
A grey ball the size of a hen's egg. Thrown, it fills a warehouse with thick smoke that you can see through and nobody else can.
A red glass bottle. For one hour after drinking it you have the strength of fifty and feel no pain at all. Any injuries you took during the hour are felt in full when it ends.
An acorn that is warm to the touch. Planted and watered, it becomes a square mile of old forest in the time it takes to walk out from under it.
A folded sheet with a seal nobody recognises and everybody respects. Shown once, it gets you and your party through any gate, checkpoint or border in the city, and then the page is blank.
A green bottle with a cork wired down. Smash it and a full gale with rain and lightning breaks over the town for an hour, centred wherever the glass landed.
A thimble of grey ash that is always warm. Scattered over someone who died within the hour, it brings them back, whole and coughing. The thimble refills on the anniversary.
A black loaf as heavy as a cobblestone. Eat it, and for one day you stand two hundred feet tall, with the strength and the appetite to match. Your clothes do not grow with you.
A small bottle, enough to write one name. Whoever's true name you write with it must answer one summons from you, from anywhere in the region, and come as fast as they honestly can.
A gold coin stamped with a palm. Give it to anyone and they will do you one favour that is within their power, however large, and hold no grudge about it afterward.
A honey-coloured liquor in a stone jar. Poured on the ground at midwinter, it gives a whole country one more month of summer: thaw, growth, harvest and all.
A sealed iron drum about the size of a wine cask, with a clockwork fuse. It destroys a city and leaves the ground clean enough to build on. The fuse can be set for anything from a minute to a year.
One bottle from a vineyard that no longer exists. Everyone who shares it with you at a table will keep faith with you and with each other for a year and a day, whatever it costs them.
Three drops of clear water in a quartz vial. One drop cures any disease, wound or poison in a single person. Three in a reservoir cures a nation of a plague.
A sliver of something golden on a silver dish. Whoever eats it stops ageing, heals from anything short of ashes, and becomes as strong as a natural disaster. The dish refills once a decade.
A fist-sized rock that hums. Thrown down, it breaks into a storm that covers a continent for a week. You choose beforehand whether it brings rain or ruin.
A pinch of silver sand in a paper fold. Thrown into the wind, it puts every living thing on a continent to sleep for a hundred years, unharmed and unaged. You are not affected.
A blue-green bead. Dropped onto a dead planet or moon, it gives it air, seas, soil and the beginnings of forests within a year.
One cup of light. Drink it, and for a day you have the power of the sun that a world orbits. Poured out over a world that has lost its sun, it gives that world one more day of light and warmth.
A lead flask that is too bright to look at even when closed. Opened, it is an exploding star, wherever you opened it. The stopper has a one-day delay so you can get clear.
A black bottle. Name one thing as you pour it out, and everyone in the galaxy forgets that the thing ever existed. Written records of it survive.
A single blank leaf torn from the back of the archive's own catalogue. Whatever you write on it happens, in full, to the whole universe, once. There is one page and there is no restock.
One mug of hot chocolate, already at drinking temperature. Whoever drinks it feels that things will probably be all right. There is one a day.
A single wooden match that lights first time on any surface, in rain or wind. The box has another one in it an hour later.
An amber sweet that restores a lost voice for an evening. Singers, auctioneers and people with a lot of apologising to do swear by them.
A blue bottle the size of a thumb. It gives eight hours of dreamless sleep to whoever drinks it and leaves no headache behind. It also works stirred into soup.
A small flask of warm, scented oil. Rubbed into skin, it doubles sexual sensation there for an hour. One flask covers two bodies.
A hard grey biscuit that tastes of nothing and feeds a soldier for three days. It never goes stale.
A black taper. While it burns, the dead of the house can be seen and spoken with. It burns for one hour.

A ruby liqueur with two small glasses. Two people who drink it together lose all embarrassment about sex with each other until dawn, and each can feel exactly what the other is enjoying. It does nothing for two people who do not already want each other.
A bright metal bead. Swallow it and you move at three times your speed for five minutes, with time enough to dodge a bullet you saw being aimed. You will be starving afterward.
A pale wine with no smell. Anyone who drinks a glass cannot tell a lie until they have slept.

A thick golden draught. For one night the drinker stays hard or wet for as long as they want, can come ten times and recovers in moments, whatever their age or health. Elderly dukes have paid a manor for one dose.
A stone flask of grey dust. Pour it in a line and a rampart thirty feet high rises along it for half a mile, with a walkway and a gate.
A pinch of silver powder. Throw it over a group of up to twenty and nobody can see or hear them for an hour. They can still see each other, so nobody has to walk into anybody.
Crack the shell and a banquet for two hundred lays itself out, with tables, linen, roast meats and musicians. Everything but the memory folds away at midnight.

A rose-coloured draught. For one night the drinker can see who in the region wants to have sex with them, and how badly, as a glow in each person's direction. It creates no desire that was not already there.
A grey pebble. Thrown as high as you can throw, it brings three days of steady, soaking rain to an entire region, enough to end a drought.
A dark, bitter brew. For a day you are a bear the size of a barn, with your own mind and its strength. You come back to yourself at dawn, with no clothes.
A folded sheet of little paper soldiers. Cut the string and five thousand of them stand up at full size, armed and drilled. They fight until the next rain and are paper again after it.

A single clear drop in a crystal vial. It passes by touch from one lover to the next across a country, and everyone it reaches has the strongest orgasms of their life that night, as many as they like. The vial refills in a year.
A cask of spirit that smokes when the bung is drawn. A sip lets you breathe fire that burns a path across a country. The cask holds forty sips.
A cone of grey incense. Breathe it and you see the next year of a country as plainly as a map, including every part of it that could still be changed.
A jar of white ointment, enough for one army. Anyone anointed with it cannot be wounded for a day.

An amphora that never runs dry on the night it is opened. Everyone across the continent who drinks your toast loses their sexual inhibitions until sunrise and has sex with whoever they want who wants them back, in beds, fields and streets. Nobody does anything they would have refused sober.
A ball of black clay the size of a marble. Bury it, walk a long way off, and say the word. A continent's worth of ground shakes, as hard and as long as you planned.
A silver bowl of something cool and white. Whoever drinks it has the moon's own power for a month: tides, madness, and the turning of beasts into people and back.
A green vial. Poured into the sea, it gives every person on the planet the power to breathe water for a generation. Coastlines stop being borders and the map doubles in size.
A glass rod that holds every storm currently raging on the planet. Break it and they all arrive in one place together, as one bolt.
A vial of liquid that looks like the night sky. Whoever drinks it becomes a living star for a century, shining, deathless and able to cross the galaxy on their own light.
A clay jar sealed with white wax. Open it, and for one year no thinking being in the galaxy can raise a hand in anger.
One bottle of the ink the first word was written in. Whatever you write with it is, and has always been, part of how the universe works. There is enough in the bottle for a single paragraph.
A brown mouse that lives in your coat pocket and will not live anywhere else. It is clean, quiet, and very fond of cheese rinds.
A grey pigeon that follows you from rooftop to rooftop and watches what you do. It coos sharply when you are about to make a mistake, and it is right about half the time.
A fat green toad that sits where you put it and eats every fly in the room. It grows a little larger every year, with no limit.
A knee-high house spirit in a wool cap who sweeps, mends and banks the fire while you sleep. It leaves for good if thanked aloud. Leave it a dish of cream as payment.
A big black dog that can swim any river with a full-grown person holding its collar.
A crow that carries small things and short messages to anyone you name within a day's flight, and brings back whatever they hand it. It expects something shiny per trip.
A moth the size of a dinner plate with wings that glow as bright as a streetlamp. It leads you toward whatever you have lost and away from whatever is hunting you.
A clockwork dog of brass and leather, wound once a week. It tracks by the sound of footsteps, never sleeps, and bites through a fence post.
A sharp-tongued woman of sixty with a basket of roots and thirty years of village cures. She treats illness and injury, knows the local plants, and looks after you whether or not you asked.
A shaggy goat that climbs sheer rock with a rider and two packs aboard.
A harbour seal that is a grey-coated stranger on land for as long as it likes. In the water it outpaces any ship, and it knows every wreck along the coast and what went down in each.
A retired drill sergeant with a bad knee and forty years of campaigns. Give him a month and a town's worth of volunteers and he hands you back a company that holds its line.
A boar as tall as a carthorse with a ridge of bramble growing along its spine. It goes through walls, hedges and cavalry in the same way, without slowing.
A thin figure in ink-stained sleeves, on loan from the archive's staff. It can find any document that exists in a city within the day.
Three hundred crows that fly as one bird. Where they circle, the weather turns to whatever you asked of them, across a whole province, and holds until they land.
A suit of soot-black plate with nobody inside and a voice like a banked fire. It can hold a bridge against a regiment.
A wandering exorcist with a paper umbrella and a habit of sleeping in. She walks between any two shrines in the region in nine steps and seals what should not be loose with slips of red paper.
A sixty-foot walking engine built for moving mountainsides. It follows spoken instructions literally, so they have to be given with care.
A blind white serpent a mile long that swims through rock as if it were water. It comes when you stamp three times and will carry you under a whole country in a night.
A grey-haired administrator who has run four kingdoms for four absent monarchs and kept all of them solvent. They will run your realm for you, or build you one within a year if you have none.

A hawk made of noon light with a wingspan that shades a village. Its stoop burns a road-wide furrow across a county, and it will carry you between any two cities in the time it takes to say their names.
Ten thousand soldiers from a war nobody won, still in ranks, still waiting for orders. They do not eat, tire or retreat.
The largest thing in any sea. Whole fleets have mistaken its back for an island and anchored there. It surfaces when you call from a shore, and it will carry a navy on its back or sink one.

A tall woman in grey who is present in every dream on the continent at once. She can carry a message, a warning or a nightmare to any sleeper you name, and she tells you what they were dreaming before she arrived.
